environment.clearanceNote: CLEARANCE is the real production default (DEFAULT_CLEARANCE = 0.05, wwwroot/extensions/ClashFinderExtension.js:60), in this model's own units -- not a value chosen to make any verdict come out a particular way.
environment.fixtureNote: The same real 3-discipline federated Revit host+links package run-gate-m2.mjs uses (Architecture/Structure/Mechanical, each independently translated, sharing one real coordinate system) -- NOT a same-URN-twice substitution. Architecture loaded first (normally), Structure and Mechanical loaded as-additional via #keep-current-models. Federated target scope: viewer.getAllModels().map(m => ({model: m})) -- ALL three currently loaded models.

blasInstrumentationNote: blasBuilt and blasCacheHits are hardcoded to 0 in every Statistics object this library produces (a pre-existing M1-era limitation, unrelated to clearance) -- they do NOT mean no BLAS work happened. The cold runs' large narrowPhaseMs values include real, uninstrumented BLAS-build cost for every geometry touched on first access.

m1_m2_candidateCountsAndReduction.candidateReductionRatioPlainly: TLAS examined 1978 clearance candidates where linear examined 7471 -- a 3.78x reduction (TLAS looked at 26.5% as many candidates as linear).

m3_precheckVsDistanceQuerySplit.note: clearanceOverlapPrechecksRun counts candidates whose AABBs touched (aabbMinDistance == 0), for which the Hard-Clash exclusion precheck actually ran volumeOverlapQuery; a candidate with disjoint-but-near AABBs returns 'skip-precheck' and is never counted. clearanceDistanceQueriesRun counts the actual clearanceQuery() calls -- one per captured production span.

m7_allSevenClearanceStatisticsFields.note: clearanceExpandedCandidatePairs is a TLAS-path-only counter (CollisionWorld.js:2058) and reads 0 on a linear run by construction -- reported here as measured, not silently omitted.

singleCallSpanDisposition.verdict: GO — worst single-call span within frameBudgetMs
singleCallSpanDisposition.spanSource: collision/CollisionWorld.js:2321 -- reportSpan('clearance-distance-query', distanceQueryMs), the real production instrumentation wrapped around every clearanceQuery() call, captured here via setSpanRecorder(CheckpointRecorder.asSpanRecorder()) from collision/scheduler.js. NOT a re-timing performed by this script.
singleCallSpanDisposition.spanScope: Union of all four measured runs (tlas-cold, tlas-warm, linear-cold, linear-warm). The unmeasured Step 3 warm-up installs no span recorder, so none of its calls can contribute.
singleCallSpanDisposition.dispositionCaveat: This is a REPORTED finding, not a CI gate: this script never fails a build on the verdict, and never retunes a shipped constant on its own initiative. Per the M3 spec a genuine NO-GO does not by itself block M3 -- a tighter DEFAULT_CLEARANCE, or scoping Soft Clash to smaller selections, may be sufficient mitigation.

correctnessCrossCheck.note: Signature-set equality is checked over the full {sourceModelTag, sourceDbId, targetModelTag, targetDbId, clashType} tuple for every returned pair, not merely pairs.length; the reported per-pair distance is compared separately as a max absolute delta over the shared keys. As in run-gate-m2.mjs: this proves the two paths agree on the final dbId-AGGREGATED clearance result, NOT that they retested an identical underlying per-fragment candidate set (this script does not capture per-fragment candidate identity).

linearCold.linearPathNote: clearanceExpandedCandidatePairs and every tlas* field read 0 on a linear run BY CONSTRUCTION (only _runClearanceTlasBroadPhase increments them, CollisionWorld.js:2029-2078) -- not a measurement failure, and deliberately not checked here.

narrowPhaseBudgetHeadroom.note: Evidence for the provisional constant, not a proposed revision -- this gate reports, it does not retune shipped defaults. Measured from ONE source instance (sourceFragmentCount=1); a multi-instance Soft Clash selection scales this count roughly with source-instance count, so the headroom shown here is not the headroom a large selection would see.

gateAnswer.question: M3 spec §17: on a realistic federated case, what does clearance mode actually cost -- (a) TLAS vs linear clearance broad-phase candidate volume, and (b) the duration of a single clearanceQuery call against frameBudgetMs?
gateAnswer.singleCallSpanDispositionSummary: GO — worst single-call span within frameBudgetMs

clearanceCandidateReduction.description: broadPhasePairs on each path -- the mode-agnostic field both clearance broad phases increment at the same point (linear: CollisionWorld.js:1966; TLAS: :2057), and therefore the directly comparable clearance candidate-search cost between them.
clearanceCandidateReduction.lowerBoundNote: Measured with exactly ONE source instance (sourceFragmentCount=1). Linear cost scales as sourceCount x targetCount; TLAS traversal cost does not scale the same way (each source instance queries the SAME already-built target TLAS). This ratio is therefore a LOWER BOUND on the reduction a multi-instance Soft Clash selection would see -- stated as a bound, never extrapolated to a specific larger number.

rawTlasPrimitiveExpansion.description: Upstream of the target-scope/self-exclusion filters -- the raw per-primitive expansion the TLAS traversal itself incurs before filtering. Reported separately so the filtered ratio above is not misread as total search-cost reduction: TLAS pays real cost at this earlier, unfiltered stage too.

broadPhaseElapsedBenefitWarm.description: Warm-vs-warm broadPhaseMs -- the fairest amortized comparison, since TLAS build cost is a one-time cost a single cold query never amortizes.

endToEndElapsedBenefit.description: Read broadPhaseShareOfWallClockCold before interpreting these: broad phase is the only part the two paths differ in, and on this fixture clearance narrow phase (Hard-Clash precheck + closestPointToGeometry) dominates total time -- so an end-to-end NOT_OBSERVED here mostly reflects narrow-phase noise, not a broad-phase regression.

gateAnswer.timingConfidenceCaveat: Wall-clock figures are descriptive, single-session measurements from one Playwright page, one sample per state. A sacrificial warm-up (Step 3: one unmeasured clearance TLAS query + one unmeasured clearance linear query, in throwaway worlds disposed before any measured world existed) removes the largest, cheapest-to-fix confound -- first-ever-call V8 JIT/module-initialization bias -- but residual order/GC/OS-scheduling noise from a single sample each cannot be ruled out. Candidate-count comparisons are structural and order-independent and are the more reliable evidence; the per-call span distribution is a population of thousands of samples, so its percentiles are far better supported than any single wall-clock number here.
